{{external media | width = 210px | float = right | headerimage=  | video1 = [http://www.laskerfoundation.org/awards/show/hepatitis-c-replicon-system-and-drug-development/#michael-j-sofia “Acceptance Remarks, 2016 Lasker Awards Ceremony”], Lasker Foundation, 2016.}}

'''Michael J. Sofia''' is a chemist whose main research focus is [[hepatitis C virus]] and [[hepatitis B virus]] drug discovery. He was a co-recipient of the [[Lasker-DeBakey Clinical Medical Research Award]] for his work on [[hepatitis C]] in 2016<ref name="Lasker">{{cite web|url=http://www.laskerfoundation.org/awards/show/hepatitis-c-replicon-system-and-drug-development/#michael-j-sofia|title=Hepatitis C replicon system and drug development - The Lasker Foundation|website=The Lasker Foundation}}</ref> and of the Gertrude B. Elion Memorial Award from the [[International Society for Antiviral Research]] in 2017.<ref name="Third"/>

==Career==

Sofia earned a bachelor's degree in chemistry from [[Cornell University]], and Ph.D. in [[organic chemistry]] from the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]].<ref name="acs">{{cite web |title=Sofia, Michael |url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/acs-webinars/presenters/sofia-michael.html |website=American Chemical Society |accessdate=13 May 2020 |language=en}}</ref> He did a postdoctoral fellow at [[Columbia University]], followed by work as a research scientist at biotech companies including the [[Squibb Institute for Medical Research]]. [[Eli Lilly and Company]], and [[Bristol-Myers Squibb]].<ref name="pnas">{{cite journal |last1=Palese |first1=Peter |title=Profile of Charles M. Rice, Ralf F. W. Bartenschlager, and Michael J. Sofia, 2016 Lasker–DeBakey Clinical Medical Research Awardees |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |pages=13934–13937 |language=en |doi=10.1073/pnas.1616592113 |date=6 December 2016|volume=113 |issue=49 |pmid=27864510 |pmc=5150379 |doi-access=free |bibcode=2016PNAS..11313934P }}</ref> He was Senior Vice President of Chemistry at [[Pharmasset]] from 2005 to 2012 when Pharmasset was acquired by [[Gilead Sciences|Gilead]], after which he became a senior advisor.

Michael J. Sofia is currently the Chief Scientific Officer and co-founder of [[Arbutus Biopharma]], formerly as OnCore Biopharma prior to its 2015 merger with Tekmira Pharmaceuticals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1447028/000117184315000197/exh_993.htm|title=Tekmira Pharmaceuticals and OnCore Biopharma Announce Merger Agreement to Create Leading Global Hepatitis B Virus Company|website=www.sec.gov}}</ref>

==Awards==
Michael J. Sofia was awarded the 2016 [[Lasker-DeBakey Clinical Medical Research Award]] for his research on [[hepatitis C]], along with [[Charles M. Rice]] and [[Ralf F. W. Bartenschlager]].<ref name="Lasker"/>
He was also awarded the 2016 IUPAC-Richter Prize in Medicinal Chemistry<ref name="IUPAC">{{cite web|url=https://iupac.org/michael-j-sofia-ph-d-is-awarded-the-2016-iupac-richter-prize/|title=Michael J. Sofia, Ph.D. is Awarded the 2016 IUPAC-Richter Prize - IUPAC - International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry|date=2 March 2016|publisher=IUPAC}}</ref> and the Economist's 2015 Innovation Award in the Bioscience category for the development of [[sofosbuvir]], which was named after Sofia for his contributions to the discovery and development of the drug.<ref name="Gounder">{{cite magazine|first=Celine |last=Gounder|title=A Better Treatment for Hepatitis C |date=December 9, 2013|magazine=The New Yorker |url=http://www.newyorker.com/tech/elements/a-better-treatment-for-hepatitis-c?currentPage=all}}</ref>  He received the Gertrude B. Elion Memorial Award of the [[International Society for Antiviral Research]] (2017).<ref name="Third">{{cite book |editor-last1=Vere Hodge |editor-first1=R. Anthony |title=The International Society for Antiviral Research: The Third Decade 2008-2017 |date=2019 |publisher=International Society for Antiviral Research |url=https://www.isar-icar.com/resources/Documents/ISAR%203rd%20Decade%20Book%20Final%20050719.pdf}}</ref>{{rp|11}}
